In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nostalgia about a positive encounter with a person who is mentally ill may help reduce stigma toward persons with mental illness by increasing social connectedness, IOGS, and outgroup trust.

this study shows that nostalgia about an interaction with a mentally-ill person improves attitudes towards the mentally ill by increasing feelings of social connection, which in turn leads to increased inclusion of the out-group into the self, and finally increased trust in the out-group.

the findings of this study show that nostalgia can be an intrapersonally effective means of warding of the stigmatization that persons with mental illness often experience, and this effect is mediated by the inclusion of the out-group (i.e., the person with a mental illness) in the self.
